summary.text: Saint Andrew is remembered as a fool-for-Christ in Constantinople and as a witness to the vision associated with the Protection of the Mother of God.

blocks.text: The OCA’s ecclesiastical life identifies him as a Slav living in tenth-century Constantinople. It describes an early attachment to Scripture and church life. Details about his formation are presented within a received Saint’s life.

blocks.text: According to the narrative, a dream called him to a distinctive ascetic life. He lived in ragged clothing and endured mockery, beatings, hunger, and exposure. The account emphasizes that he passed the alms he received to people in need.

blocks.text: The life places Saint Andrew’s death in 936. It describes many hardships but does not say that he was executed as a martyr. The date follows this ecclesiastical tradition.

blocks.text: His best-known story is the vision at the Blachernae church of the Theotokos extending her veil over those present. The life connects that account with the October 1 feast of her Protection; his own feast is October 2.
